html:
Sigiriya, "Lion Rock", is a granite rock about 180 metres high in central Sri Lanka, crowned by the ruins of a palace. King Kashyapa I made it his fortress and capital, ruling from about 477 to 495.

According to the chronicle Culavamsa, Kashyapa seized the throne of Anuradhapura by killing his father, King Dhatusena. Fearing his half-brother Moggallana, who had fled to India, he moved to this rock. Visitors climbed to the top through the paws of a giant brick lion, of which only the paws remain.

  • Frescoes of graceful women, perhaps heavenly maidens, survive in a sheltered pocket of the rock face.
  • A polished plaster "mirror wall" carries hundreds of short poems scratched by visitors from about the 8th century on, some of the earliest writing in Sinhala.
  • Below lie symmetrical water gardens, with pools and fountains still fed in the rainy season.

Moggallana returned with an army in 495, and Kashyapa died in battle. The capital went back to Anuradhapura, and the rock became a Buddhist monastery. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Sri Lanka's best-known monument.
sum: Sigiriya, "Lion Rock", is a granite rock about 180 metres high in central Sri Lanka, crowned by the ruins of a palace. King Kashyapa I made it his fortress and capital, ruling from about 477 to 495.
